stem: A client recovering from acute ischemic stroke has motor weakness, difficulty with activities of daily living, dysarthria, and cognitive changes. Why is interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment important?

options.A: Stroke can produce different combinations of physical, functional, communication, cognitive, and psychosocial impairments, so coordinated multidisciplinary assessment helps determine the appropriate rehabilitation needs and level of care.
options.B: A single discipline can reliably address every post-stroke impairment, making coordinated rehabilitation assessment unnecessary.
options.C: Only motor weakness affects rehabilitation planning; communication, cognition, swallowing, and activities of daily living do not alter the rehabilitation plan.
options.D: Rehabilitation assessment should generally be deferred until after discharge because in-hospital interdisciplinary evaluation has no association with functional recovery.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline notes that patients have highly variable impairments and individualized needs and recommends a comprehensive multidisciplinary approach to determine the appropriate intensity and modality of rehabilitation. In-hospital interdisciplinary rehabilitation evaluation is associated with improved functional outcomes. B and C ignore the multidimensional effects of stroke. D contradicts the guideline's support for inpatient interdisciplinary assessment and early rehabilitation planning.
educational_objective: Coordinate early interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment after stroke because recovery needs can span mobility, self-care, communication, swallowing, cognition, and psychosocial function and require an individualized plan and appropriate post-acute level of care.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_locator: Section 5.7 Rehabilitation — Synopsis: patients with stroke have highly variable degrees of impairment and diverse individualized needs; a comprehensive multidisciplinary program is critical for assessing appropriate rehabilitation intensity and modality. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 1: organized stroke units commonly include interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment; inpatient interdisciplinary evaluation for the appropriate level of rehabilitation is associated with improved functional outcomes and guidelines support multidisciplinary inpatient evaluation.
source_claim_supported: Post-stroke rehabilitation planning should use multidisciplinary assessment because impairments and recovery needs vary across functional domains; inpatient interdisciplinary evaluation helps determine the appropriate rehabilitation level and is associated with improved functional recovery.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, coordinate referrals and transitions, and plan care across functional needs.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interdisciplinary post-stroke rehabilitation planning
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw broad claim into an individualized rehabilitation-planning scenario anchored to the current 2026 AHA/ASA guideline. The final item avoids attributing outcome improvement to a fixed list of disciplines or implying every stroke survivor requires identical services.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against Section 5.7 Rehabilitation of the 2026 AHA/ASA AIS guideline.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A matches the individualized multidisciplinary rehabilitation model. B falsely makes one discipline sufficient. C ignores nonmotor domains. D incorrectly defers a supported in-hospital evaluation.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; multidomain deficits require individualized interdisciplinary planning.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; communication, cognition, swallowing and ADLs materially affect planning.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; inpatient rehabilitation assessment is supported and associated with better outcomes.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reflects the guideline without assuming that every client needs the same disciplines or intensity.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address the rationale and timing for rehabilitation planning.
audit_findings.blueprint: Interdisciplinary coordination and transition planning fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked 2026 rehabilitation timing, multidisciplinary evaluation, early mobilization caveats, and individualized level-of-care selection. Avoided implying that very early high-dose mobilization is universally beneficial. No second answer remained.
